scope: Proposition 5.4 (Canonical entropy and endpoint recovery) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 61-62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On its domain of use, the excess satisfies E(a, v) = H(a, v) − D0 − (p + d)a − W(a, v) ≥ 0. (canon) For hybrid names this assertion is used only when g = 0, w < 0, and at their terminal limits by continuity. The following equality and prediction statements also hold, with lists of size s−o(1). (i) For D = 1, g = 0, equality holds at (1, 0). In the classical equality and pure linear cases with b′ 1 > 0, equality holds at v = u(a). In a classical strict family ending at D, it holds at (D, u(D)). At these equality points use the template with l = b + v = b1, or the pure linear template. (ii) In a strict family every row connected from i < D to D, and its label, predicts k̄. After its subtraction, |Ki| ≤ sb2(D)−D−o(1) , |βD(TD) − βi(Ti)| ≤ sb(i)−o(1) . 61 (iii) In an equality or pure linear family, suppose J > 0, a < j < 1, v = u(j) > 0, and l(a, v) ≤ min [j,1] b1. Then λj predicts C(a, v) on every completing path; in the hybrid case require w < 0. (iv) In the classical cases with b′ 1 > 0, fix 0 < a < j. If v − u(j) ≥ 0 is sufficiently small compared with j − a and l(a, v) ≤ b1(j), then (λj, X(v)) predicts C(a, v). The strict version uses j = D. There λD alone suffices at v = u(D); this last assertion also holds for hybrid D = 1 and w < 0, without the condition b′ 1 > 0. No equality is asserted at an arbitrary point where min[a,1] b1 < b1(a).
